paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the people didn't wait for God, so they made a god they could see. Moses was delayed, and the crowd couldn't stand the silence (Exodus 32:1). Then Aaron shaped their gold into a calf, and they said, "These, O Israel, are your gods, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt!" (Exodus 32:4). That's the trap, baker: when God feels quiet, we grab something we can hold and give it His credit.

Now look at the part that matters most. The LORD's anger burned, and the people truly deserved to hear it (Exodus 32:9-10). But Moses stood in the gap and pleaded, and the LORD relented from the calamity He had threatened (Exodus 32:11-14). Later Moses even said, "if You would only forgive their sin.... But if not, please blot me out of the book that You have written." (Exodus 32:32). I think that's a man who loved his people enough to put himself on the line for them.

But sin is not small, and this passage won't let us treat it that way. Aaron said the calf just came out of the fire (Exodus 32:24), and I'm telling you, friend, nobody has ever baked a good excuse (and I've tried). The LORD said, "Whoever has sinned against Me, I will blot out of My book." (Exodus 32:33). So the lesson is to wait on God, own what you've done, and thank Him for the One who pleads for us. This story isn't over.
